name: Armenian

ancestors.notes: Isolated Indo-European branch; Armenian alphabet created by Mesrop Mashtots in 405 CE

notes: Eastern Armenian (standard). Armenian alphabet (Aybuben) has 38 letters. Digraph ու = /u/. Letters ե and ո have positional allophones: word-initial ե = /jɛ/, medial = /ɛ/; word-initial ո = /vo/, medial = /o/. Aspirated stops (թ, չ, փ, ք, ց) vs plain voiced (բ, գ, դ) vs plain voiceless (կ, պ, տ).

sources.author: Dum-Tragut, Jasmine
sources.title: Armenian: Modern Eastern Armenian

sources.notes: Reference grammar of Modern Eastern Armenian. Confirmed via Crossref metadata (DOI 10.1075/loall.14) and publisher ISBN listing as a real, published grammar; not independently paged. Cited for the positional allophony of ե and ո (word-initial [jɛ]/[vo] vs. medial [ɛ]/[o]) and the three-way aspirated/plain-voiced/plain-voiceless stop contrast that this spec's notes describe -- claims consistent with the standard descriptive treatment of Eastern Armenian phonology, though the specific page ranges were not opened.
